No fixed count or scheme (poets.org free verse glossary); the engine only measures.
poets.org haiku: three lines of 5/7/5. The same source notes contemporary practice routinely breaks 5/7/5, so the counts are soft.
poets.org limerick: five lines AABBA, anapestic; lines 1, 2 and 5 have three feet, lines 3 and 4 two.
poets.org ballad: quatrains rhymed ABCB or ABAB, three or four stresses per line. That stress count is a definition only: no check enforces it, because scansion of stress counts is contested.
poets.org sonnet: 14 lines of iambic pentameter; Shakespearean = three quatrains and a couplet, ababcdcdefefgg.

poets.org sonnet: 14 lines of iambic pentameter; Petrarchan = octave abbaabba and sestet cdecde or cdcdcd, with the volta after line 8 (the turn). The volta is a definition only: no check enforces it.
poets.org villanelle: 19 lines, five tercets and a quatrain, two refrains. Uppercase scheme letters are refrain lines; A1 and A2 repeat verbatim at the listed lines.
poets.org sestina: six six-line stanzas on six rotating end words (ABCDEF, FAEBDC, CFDABE, ECBFAD, DEACFB, BDFECA) and a three-line envoi holding all six.

Weak support: the sources are course descriptions (Pattison/Berklee topics) and a practitioner article (Musical U); no authoritative definition of song structure was found. Sections come from headings.
